title: How To Be Mentally Tougher
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin offers six disciplines to build the mental toughness he considers essential for effective, calm teaching: sitting in silence, turning off your phone, reading for extended periods, exercising without media distraction, taking cold showers, and intermittent fasting. He frames each as a way to strengthen impulse control and resilience, arguing that a teacher swayed easily by their phone will likely be swayed just as easily by students. Cold showers and fasting are described as producing physical benefits alongside mental toughness through delayed gratification and discomfort tolerance, though he advises checking with a doctor before attempting the more physically demanding disciplines. The article recommends starting with just one discipline and sustaining it for at least two weeks to overcome initial resistance. It closes by tying these practices to broader wellbeing, not just classroom leadership.
points: Six disciplines are recommended for building mental toughness: sitting in silence, turning off your phone, reading more, exercising without distraction, cold showers, and fasting.
A teacher who is easily swayed by phone and screen impulses is likely to be similarly swayed by student pushback in the classroom.
Cold showers are described as triggering brain chemicals that counteract discomfort, leaving a person calmer afterward.
Fasting builds mental strength through delayed gratification, a trait linked to broader success.
Starting with just one discipline and sustaining it for at least two weeks is recommended to overcome initial resistance and build the habit.
quotes: To be an effective teacher in this day and age, you’ve got to be mentally tough.
Slow your body and your mind will follow. If you’re swayed by the pull of your phone, then you’ll likely be more easily swayed by your students.
According to research, the pain of cold showers triggers chemicals in the brain that counteract the discomfort, leaving you calmer and happier for hours afterward.
The mental strength comes from delaying gratification, which has been shown to correlate with success.
Start with just one idea above and stick with it for at least two weeks. It may take that long to overcome your resistance.
